title: Concurrent basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation and vertebral augmentation as part of a multimodal palliative plan for pathological vertebral compression fracture from spine tumor: A case series of three patients

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Concurrent basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation and vertebral augmentation as part of a multimodal palliative plan for pathological vertebral compression fracture from spine tumor: A case series of three patients》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0010】Spinal metastases are common tumors involving the spine and represent a frequent occurrence of cancer-related morbidity, with pain presenting as the hallmark symptom and a major source of functional decline [1]. Spinal metastatic disease can involve the vertebral body, pedicles, posterior elements, and epidural space, which increases pathologic vertebral compression fractures (VCF), mechanical instability, and neurologic deficits from metastatic epidural spinal cord compression (MESCC) [1].

【Introduction · p0015】For metastasis-induced VCF, percutaneous vertebral augmentation (VA) has been used as an adjunct to radiotherapy and systemic therapy to reduce pain and improve vertebral stability [2]. Despite these interventions, persistent pain is common and multifactorial, due to tumor-associated inflammation, vertebral endplate injury, and mechanical instability. The basivertebral nerve (BVN) provides the main sensory innervation to the vertebral body and endplates, and is responsible for pain signal transmission caused by endplate injury and intraosseous inflammation. Basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation (BVNRFA) is a minimally invasive procedure used to disrupt BVN-mediated nociceptive signaling and has shown significant improvements in pain reduction for patients with chronic vertebrogenic low back pain [3].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Concurrent basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation and vertebral augmentation as part of a multimodal palliative plan for pathological vertebral compression fracture from spine tumor: A case series of three patients》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · p0110】Concurrent BVNRFA and VA may be an efficacious and safe option for select patients with pathological VCF secondary to spinal tumors within a broader multidisciplinary palliative and interventional pain plan. This combined approach targets both mechanical and neurogenic pain, offering meaningful pain relief, especially in a palliative setting.

【Conclusion · abstract-3-1】Concurrent BVNRFA and VA is a novel and synergistic approach that may provide an additional option for select patients with pathological vertebral compression fractures from a spinal tumor within palliative and interventional pain settings. Larger studies are required to clarify ideal patient selection, duration of benefit, and safety.
